ratings.label: Realistic
ratings.desc: No problem with the Constitution or EU law. An ordinary law, a government decision or an affordable amount of money is enough.

ratings.label: Realistic, but harder
ratings.desc: Can be done, but needs more: an organic law (176 votes), the regions' agreement, a lot of money or several years.

ratings.label: Unlikely
ratings.desc: Big obstacles: the courts, EU law, the powers of the regions, a cost the budget cannot pay, or no majority in parliament.

ratings.label: Not possible as things stand
ratings.desc: Goes against the Constitution or EU law, or needs a change to the Constitution that cannot get the three-fifths or two-thirds majority it needs.

ratings.label: Vague
ratings.desc: No numbers, dates or plan, so nobody can check if it was done.

housing.label: Rent rules: limits, renewals, cancelling the law
Tax breaks for landlords instead of rent limits
Taxes or limits for large owners and investors
Limit who can buy or get housing

taxes.label: Income tax cuts and inflation-linked bands
Taxes on capital, wealth and big firms

pensions.label: Pensions that rise with prices, and minimum pensions

immigration.label: Help for new arrivals, and who provides it

territorial.label: Independence votes and recognition as a nation

parties.name: PP
parties.summary: Almost every promise is realistic on its own, but the whole programme does not add up. It lowers taxes and fees: income tax linked to inflation, 4% VAT, no social security fees for new self-employed people and an end to the 7% tax on electricity generation. At the same time it promises 4,500 more doctors, 50% state money for long-term care, €40 billion for water and lower public debt.
parties.doable: Most measures need only an ordinary law or a government decision. Many extend schemes that already exist, such as the ICO deposit guarantee.
parties.limits: The weakest points are the million homes (Spain now finishes about 100,000 a year), a €300 billion plan for roads, railways and other infrastructure, and cancelling the amnesty. The amnesty cannot be taken back where it has already been applied (art. 9.3 of the Constitution).

parties.name: PSOE
parties.summary: Many promises extend measures that already exist, so its ratings are high. The programme does not answer the main question for the next government: Catalonia and the conditions of ERC and Junts.
parties.doable: Examples are the minimum wage at 60% of the average wage, social security fees for the self-employed based on real income, and the public housing company CASA 47.
parties.limits: Changes to the Constitution (on housing, pensions, the Senate and *aforamientos*, the special court rules for politicians) are not possible without PP. The 37.5-hour week has already failed in Congress. Cancelling €83 billion of regional debt needs an organic law, and 176 votes are not certain. "1% of GDP for housing" and €21 billion more for the regions have no named source of money.

parties.name: Vox
parties.summary: The centre of the programme is "national priority" (*prioridad nacional*): Spanish citizens first for housing, the minimum income, schools and benefits. It also includes a tax on money sent abroad, "remigration", leaving EU climate rules, and Gibraltar. Almost a quarter of its promises have no numbers.
parties.doable: Promises that need only an ordinary or organic law and a majority are realistic: judges choosing the judges' council (CGPJ), cancelling the Housing Law and the Democratic Memory Law, and changes to the Criminal Code.
parties.limits: Most of its main promises go against art. 14 of the Constitution and EU law. Gibraltar cannot change without the UK's agreement.

parties.name: Sumar
parties.summary: One of the most expensive programmes. It promises 1% of GDP for housing, 2.3% of GDP for the regions, 3.5% for climate, 7% for education, 8% for health and €200 per child. In our estimate that is over €100 billion a year, more than its new taxes would bring in.
parties.doable: Tax changes by ordinary law, such as a minimum company tax of 20% and a wider wealth tax. Also practical steps for migrants, such as easier town-hall registration and a basic bank account.
parties.limits: Taking homes from large owners, banning home purchases by people who will not live in them, and bringing the power grids under state ownership go against art. 33 of the Constitution and EU law.

parties.name: Podemos
parties.summary: It has the most D ratings of any party (15): a 40% rent cut, a ban on buying homes you will not live in, a republic, an end to the King's legal immunity, and neutrality. Leaving NATO, a basic income for everyone, retirement at 63 and a 30-hour week are blocked by money and missing votes (C), not by the law.
parties.doable: Specific measures: putting short-term rentals under normal rental law, ending the Beckham regime, lower VAT on services and paid internships.
parties.limits: Its main housing promises go against the right to property (art. 33) and the EU rule on free movement of money.

parties.name: ERC
parties.summary: Its most realistic promises are those it could win in a deal in Congress: cancelling regional *FLA* debt, the Rodalies commuter trains and the "gag law" (*ley mordaza*).
parties.doable: Promises that can pass through a deal in Congress: debt relief, moving commuter trains to Catalonia, and tax changes on investment income and tourist rentals.
parties.limits: An independence referendum goes against the Constitution. A funding deal like the Basque one, a Catalan minimum wage, and moving immigration and rental powers to Catalonia run into art. 149 of the Constitution and Constitutional Court decisions.

parties.name: Junts
parties.summary: On the economy it is centre-right: no rent limits, more tax deductions and tax breaks. But its main promises are about Catalonia's powers: its own tax agreement, its own social security, control of the Schengen border, and the Catalan high court as the final court.
parties.doable: Tax cuts and incentives for landlords to rent out homes, by ordinary law.
parties.limits: The Constitution mostly does not allow its plans for Catalonia's powers (Constitutional Court decision of 2010 on the Statute).

parties.name: EH Bildu
parties.summary: It mixes realistic social measures, such as stable rents and action on tourist flats, with promises to recognise nations, a right to decide independence, leaving NATO and ending EU budget rules.
parties.doable: Rental rules by ordinary law, such as automatic contract renewal and limits on yearly rent rises.
parties.limits: Recognising nations and a right to decide independence need a change to the Constitution. Ending EU budget rules needs the other EU countries to agree, and removing art. 135 also needs a change to the Constitution. A regional minimum wage would need the state to change labour law (the Workers' Statute).

parties.name: PNV
parties.summary: Many of its promises carry out the Basque Statute of Gernika and the *concierto*, the Basque tax agreement. Part of this work is already under way through joint commissions.
parties.doable: Small tax changes within EU rules, pension measures, and powers moved to the Basque Country through joint commissions.
parties.limits: Recognition as a "nation" and a separate Basque minimum wage are not realistic.

parties.name: BNG
parties.summary: A short programme of 10 commitments with few numbers. It mixes realistic social measures with recognising Galicia as a nation, leaving NATO and a regional minimum wage.
parties.doable: Protection for tenants and limits on tourist and short-term rentals.
parties.limits: Recognition as a nation and a right to decide independence need a change to the Constitution. The pension and working-week promises lack money or votes.

parties.name: CC
parties.summary: Almost all its promises are about money and carrying out the Canary Islands Statute and the islands' special tax system (*REF*). Most of them could come through talks in Congress, where CC's votes can decide a majority.
parties.doable: Tax breaks for the islands, the 75% travel discount for residents and rules on holiday rentals. Most of these extend what already exists.
parties.limits: One point is disputed: limiting home purchases by foreigners. EU law does not allow this for EU citizens.
